payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-06-03
payload.summary:
**AI agents eat the work stack**: Codex expands from devs into knowledge work, Claude Code adds workflows, Gemini exposes Thinking Levels; **yes-code vs no-code** becomes the new platform fight as Vercel, Replit, OpenClaw, and enterprise sandboxes race to make agent-built apps deployable; **Listen Labs reframes market research**: thousands of AI voice interviews, emotion signals, traceable clips, and customer simulation turn “ask users” from slow theater into live product radar.

**智能体开始吞掉工作流**：Codex 走出开发者圈，Claude Code 加上 workflows，Gemini 把 Thinking Levels 放到全端；**no-code 被 yes-code 反杀**：Vercel、Replit、OpenClaw 都在抢“让智能体写完就能上线”的底座；**Listen Labs 把用户调研改成雷达**：AI 同时跑上千个语音访谈，看表情、留证据、回连销售数据，比问卷狠多了。

sections.headline: Simple SaaS is harder to monetize now · 简单 SaaS 现在更难变现
sections.body:
People are saying SaaS is not dead.

I think larger enterprise SaaS that can do multiple jobs are probably fine (e.g., Figma).

But if you’re building a simple SaaS for a narrow use case, I think it's harder to monetize now because:

1.  AI skills can often solve the same problem in a much more flexible, personalized way.

2.  AI-native agents like Codex / Claude Code that have a user's personal context and memory have far more knowledge to solve the user's problem vs. a standalone SaaS website or chatbot.

3.  People are willing to pay hundreds or thousands for services (human touch is what's rare these days) but charge $20 / month for a SaaS and people will compare it's value to their Claude / ChatGPT subscription.

Curious if others feel the same way? I guess I'm in a bubble and most people have not set up their own AI skills yet.

大家都在说 **SaaS** 没死。

我觉得能处理多种工作的、大型企业级 **SaaS** 应该没问题，比如 **Figma**。

但如果你做的是面向窄场景的简单 **SaaS**，我觉得现在变现更难了，原因是：

1.  **AI skills** 往往能用更灵活、更个性化的方式解决同一个问题。

2.  像 **Codex** / **Claude Code** 这样的 AI-native agents，掌握用户的个人上下文和记忆。相比一个独立的 **SaaS** 网站或聊天机器人，它们更懂用户的问题。

3.  人们愿意为服务付几百、几千美元，因为现在稀缺的是人的触感。但如果一个 **SaaS** 收 20 美元/月，用户就会拿它的价值去和自己的 **Claude** / **ChatGPT** 订阅比。

好奇其他人是不是也有同感？也可能是我在同温层里，毕竟多数人还没配置自己的 **AI skills**。

sections.headline: YES-CODE: coding agents make code abundant / YES-CODE：编程智能体让代码变得充裕
sections.body:
YES-CODE

An entire category of software, "no-code", was built under the presumption that code is expensive, difficult, and scarce.

Coding agents have forever changed the equation. Code is now cheap, easy, and abundant.

I remember @cramforce being asked by an analyst long ago: "soo, is @vercel like a no-code platform?" Without hesitation he goes "no, it's the absolute opposite. It's a yes-code platform." 😁

A key thing we set out to do was to be uncompromising in quality and sophistication of the things you could host. No-code solutions took shortcuts and set hard ceilings, typically on performance and sophistication.

Our mission is to create the easiest cloud for agents that you never graduate from.

PS: welcome https://t.co/WTKvpexJtD to Vercel!

**YES-CODE**

过去整个「无代码」软件品类，都是建立在一个前提上：代码昂贵、困难、稀缺。

编程智能体已经彻底改写了这个公式。代码现在便宜、简单，而且充足。

我记得很久以前有位分析师问 @cramforce：「所以，**Vercel** 算是无代码平台吗？」他毫不犹豫地说：「不，正好相反。它是一个 yes-code 平台。」😁

我们一开始就很看重的一点，是对可托管内容的质量和复杂度不妥协。无代码方案往往会走捷径，并设置硬上限，通常卡在性能和复杂度上。

我们的使命，是为智能体打造最容易上手、也永远不需要迁移出去的云。

PS：欢迎 https://t.co/WTKvpexJtD 加入 **Vercel**！

sections.headline: Language is the API in AI education / 语言正在成为 AI 教育里的 API
sections.body:
This is what education in the age of AI looks like. Start with the language: the linguistic surface is your roadmap. Much like an SDK has a set of function definitions, human language is the new API to the world.

It also always has been… there's never been an expert in any field without mastery over its language. The distinction is that English alone could not produce tangible things. You had to translate it into machine instruction, through learning or delegation to others. You can now go direct.

这就是 **AI** 时代的教育该有的样子。先从语言开始：语言表层就是你的路线图。就像一个 **SDK** 有一组函数定义，人类语言正在成为通向世界的新 **API**。

其实它一直都是。任何领域的专家，都离不开对该领域语言的掌握。区别在于，以前单靠英语无法产出真实东西。你必须通过学习，或委托他人，把它翻译成机器指令。现在你可以直接抵达。

sections.headline: Model routing becomes inevitable as token costs grow · 随着 token 成本上升，模型路由会成为必然
sections.body:
As token budgets take on a larger part of operating expenses over time, model routing is the inevitable conclusion. This is also one of the biggest areas of differentiation for the applied AI layer over time. 

By understanding the different work patterns in your domain, and having strong evals for that domain, you’ll be able to cost/performance optimize effectively.

We’re still likely at the point where most use-cases will need frontier performance for the foreseeable future; but soon you will be able to peel off individual use-cases and send them to lower cost models once the quality is sufficient for the task.

Enterprises individually trying to figure this out themselves at scale will likely not be possible, so the products that can intelligently route these workflows to the right tier of model will be in a strong position to aggregate more demand.

随着 token 预算在运营成本里占比越来越高，模型路由会成为必然结果。这也会是应用层 **AI** 长期拉开差距的关键领域之一。

只要理解所在领域里的不同工作模式，并且有扎实的领域评测，就能有效优化成本和性能。

短期看，大多数用例可能仍然需要前沿模型的能力；但很快，一旦某些任务的质量达标，就可以把单个用例拆出来，交给成本更低的模型处理。

企业各自单独在大规模场景里摸索这件事，大概率走不通。所以，能把这些工作流智能路由到合适模型层级的产品，会处在更有利的位置，聚合更多需求。

sections.headline: Founders Need More Than One Edge · 创始人不能只押一个优势
sections.body:
The best founders treat the following as a necessary component of their business but NOT the entire business..

> AI / timing / why now
> Funding
> Distribution / hype
> Market
> Product
> Revenue

I’m seeing too many pitches that are touting only one of these as the core reason to invest. 

The bar has frankly never been higher (see the seed - A gap) and you really need to be able to explain how you’re capturing at least multiple of these in a unique way that’ll be hard for others to copy. 

Especially in overcrowded categories. Otherwise, it gets very hard for the other side (aka VC) to make a case for their own partners to write the check. 

And, founders often get frustrated because their businesses are strong. Stronger than they have ever been in the past. Why can’t people just write the check? Like why do I need to waste time fundraising? It’s because like it or not the levels do keep going up. Narrative matters, ambition matters and try to understand the opportunity cost has also never been higher on the other side. If you’re profitable and don’t need capital, then who cares. And you don’t need to optimize for VCs but you DO need to give them a reason to believe. 

So, keep your bar high. Find a capital partner that still has conviction and deserves equity in your company. But, please take those ten extra minutes to communicate your long term ambition, because that might be the only small difference between you and the next round.

最好的创始人会把下面这些视为业务的必要组成部分，但不会把其中任何一个当成全部业务：

> **AI** / 时机 / 为什么是现在
> 融资
> 分发 / 热度
> 市场
> 产品
> 收入

我最近看到太多 pitch，只拿其中一个点当作投资的核心理由。

坦白说，门槛从来没有这么高过（看看种子轮到 **A 轮**之间的断层就知道）。你真的得讲清楚：你如何以一种别人很难复制的方式，同时抓住其中多个要素。

尤其是在拥挤赛道里。否则，对另一边（也就是 **VC**）来说，要说服自己的合伙人写支票会非常难。

创始人也常常会因此沮丧，因为他们的业务确实很强。甚至比过去任何时候都强。为什么投资人不能直接写支票？为什么我还要浪费时间融资？原因是，不管你喜不喜欢，水位一直在涨。叙事重要，野心重要，也要理解投资人那边的机会成本同样从没这么高过。如果你已经盈利、不需要资本，那无所谓。你不需要围着 **VC** 优化，但你确实需要给他们一个相信你的理由。

所以，继续把标准放高。找一个仍然有信念、也配得上拿你公司股权的资本伙伴。但请多花那十分钟，把你的长期野心讲清楚，因为这点小差别，可能就是你和下一轮融资之间的距离。

sections.headline: Rechecking the Opus 4.8 read after real-world use / 真实上手后重新看 Opus 4.8
sections.body:
Almost a week later! What are your thoughts on **Opus 4.8**?

We were extremely bullish on it in testing—it seems the response was more tepid once y'all got your hands on it. If you disagreed with our take I'm curious why so we can tune our evaluations!

One theory I have is that by nature it pushes on your frame a little more, and the results are high-variance—sometimes it does something amazing, and sometimes it disagrees in a way that is obviously wrong.

But curious how you're feeling and what you're reaching for after a few days of testing

快一周了！你们怎么看 **Opus 4.8**？

我们测试时非常看好它，但大家真正上手后的反应似乎冷一些。如果你不同意我们的判断，我很想知道原因，这样我们可以调整评测方式。

我的一个猜测是，它天生更会挑战你的框架，结果波动也更大：有时能做出很惊艳的东西，有时又会用一种明显错误的方式反驳你。

不过我更想知道，你们测了几天之后现在感觉如何，实际会去用什么。

sections.headline: AI customer research at interview scale / 用 AI 把客户研究扩到访谈级规模
sections.body:
**Alfred Wahlforss**, founder and CEO of **Listen Labs**, describes the company as an AI-first customer research platform that can run thousands of voice interviews at once. Users ask a research question, **Listen Labs** generates an interview guide, recruits from a claimed audience of 30 million participants, conducts hundreds of AI-led interviews, and turns the results into recommendations.

He says the next step is simulation: after enough interviews, **Listen Labs** wants to predict how customers may answer future questions. His thesis is blunt: as building products gets easier with AI, knowing what to build becomes the harder and more valuable problem.

**Listen Labs** 创始人兼 CEO **Alfred Wahlforss** 说，这家公司做的是 AI-first 客户研究平台：能同时跑成千上万场语音访谈。用户提出一个研究问题，**Listen Labs** 自动生成访谈提纲，从号称 3000 万人的受访者池里找人，完成数百场 AI 主持的访谈，再把结果整理成建议。

下一步是“模拟”：当平台积累足够多访谈后，尝试预测客户未来会怎么回答问题。他的判断很直接：AI 会让造产品变得更容易，真正难的是知道该造什么。

sections.headline: Why interviews beat shallow surveys / 为什么深度访谈比浅层问卷更有用
sections.body:
Wahlforss argues that traditional surveys are often inconsistent, even when the same person answers the same multiple-choice question again. In contrast, he says AI-led interviews force respondents to reason through answers, producing more stable and useful signals.

He still frames A/B testing as the gold standard, but notes that many companies lack the traffic or conditions to run clean experiments. In those cases, fast customer input is better than flying blind. **Listen Labs** also compares interview findings against later sales data, such as product testing for **Chubbies**.

Wahlforss 认为，传统问卷的问题在于信号太浅。同一个人重新回答同一道选择题，结果也可能大幅摇摆。相比之下，AI 访谈会逼着受访者把想法讲清楚，答案更稳定，也更容易看出真实动机。

他承认 **A/B testing** 仍是黄金标准，但很多公司没有足够流量，也很难把实验条件做干净。这种情况下，快速拿到客户输入，总比闭门拍脑袋强。**Listen Labs** 还会把访谈结论和后续销售数据对照，比如帮 **Chubbies** 做产品测试。

sections.headline: Video, emotion, and traceability / 视频、情绪和可追溯性
sections.body:
The product experience is closer to a video call with an AI agent than a static survey. **Listen Labs** captures voice, video, facial cues, and emotion signals, which Wahlforss says helps bridge the gap between what people claim and what they actually feel.

For advertising research, he says enthusiastic reactions on video can be more predictive than high Likert-scale purchase intent scores alone. The platform is also built around traceability: every synthesized insight can be clicked back to the underlying video clip or quote, so customers can inspect where the AI’s conclusion came from.

这个产品更像是和 AI agent 开视频会，而不是填一张静态问卷。**Listen Labs** 会捕捉语音、视频、面部反应和情绪信号。Wahlforss 认为，这能拉近“嘴上怎么说”和“心里怎么想”之间的距离。

在广告研究里，他说视频里真实兴奋的反应，往往比 Likert 量表上的高购买意愿分数更有参考价值。平台也强调可追溯：每条 AI 汇总出的洞察，都能点回原始视频片段或引用，客户可以直接检查结论从哪来。

sections.headline: From viral consumer app to enterprise research platform / 从爆款消费应用转向企业研究平台
sections.body:
Wahlforss says **Listen Labs** grew out of the founders’ earlier consumer app, **Bfake**, which let users create AI avatars of themselves using fine-tuned **Stable Diffusion**. After the app went viral and gained 20,000 users overnight, the team had major churn and needed to understand why.

They built an AI interview tool for their own research: positioning, use cases, churn, and customer motivation. That internal tool became the seed for **Listen Labs**.

Wahlforss 说，**Listen Labs** 的起点是他们之前做的消费级应用 **Bfake**：用户可以用微调后的 **Stable Diffusion** 生成自己的 AI 分身。产品一夜爆火，来了 2 万用户，但流失也很严重，团队必须弄清楚原因。

于是他们先给自己做了一个 AI 访谈工具，用来研究定位、使用场景、流失原因和用户动机。后来这个内部工具变成了 **Listen Labs** 的雏形。

sections.headline: Market research moves from services to software / 市场研究从服务业变成软件能力
sections.body:
Wahlforss contrasts the old market research world with the AI-native version. Historically, companies relied on survey tools like **Qualtrics** or expensive services firms to design questions, recruit participants, run focus groups, and analyze interviews. Large companies, including **Microsoft**, may spend tens of millions of dollars on focus groups and research operations.

His view is that AI lowers the friction enough that customer input can become part of many more decisions. **Listen Labs** can return feedback from real people within minutes, run asynchronously, and reduce costs because participants can respond on their own schedule.

Wahlforss 把旧市场研究和 AI-native 研究做了对比。过去，公司要么用 **Qualtrics** 这类问卷工具，要么找昂贵的服务公司来设计问题、招募受访者、组织焦点小组、分析访谈。像 **Microsoft** 这样的大公司，可能一年在焦点小组和研究流程上花掉数千万美元。

他的观点是，AI 把和客户对话的摩擦降到足够低，客户输入就能进入更多决策。**Listen Labs** 能在几分钟内拿到真实用户反馈，异步进行，成本也更低，因为受访者可以按自己的时间完成访谈。
